node.title: Re: Interactive openssl raw
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi [Guntherssl],

From [doc://exec]:

The exec function executes a system command and never returns; use [doc://system] instead of exec if you want it to return.

If you [id://111088], normally Perl warns you about this (although not in the code you showed, as you're not using [doc://exec] in void context).

However, to communicate with a subprocess interactively, [doc://exec]/[doc://system] is not the right thing, the best way to go is use a module like [mod://IPC::Run] or perhaps [mod://Expect].

Lastly, you don't necessarily need to shell out to [man://openssl] for this, I don't see how [mod://IO::Socket::SSL] would prevent you from "watch each part manually and interact with it live".

Hope this helps,
-- Hauke D
